title: Capture and quality guide (PolyCam-class behaviour, open stack)
disclaimer: Commercial apps like PolyCam do not publish their full pipeline. This file describes standard photogrammetry and 3D Gaussian Splatting practice, and how to drive this API (SAM + MapAnything + GS) toward similar results. Your web UI can render it verbatim or map fields to localised copy.

typical_commercial_object_mode: Guided orbit capture (fixed subject, many overlapping views).
Per-view camera poses from visual-inertial / SfM with aggressive filtering.
Object-centric masking or full-scene training with strong regularisation.
NeRF or 3DGS optimisation against high-bit-depth colour targets, often with full-resolution supervision and proprietary colour pipelines.
this_backend_default: Uploads are optionally downscaled (max_input_image_side) then SAM segments the subject (black background on masked copies).
Gaussian Splatting: MapAnything feeds a COLMAP-compatible text sparse seed; official graphdeco train.py refines splats.

When gs_train_with_original_images is true (default), scene images used for the GS photometric loss are overwritten with the matching originals before train.py—geometry still uses masked-friendly views, colour supervision matches commercial-style full photos.
Mesh (.glb) path: Poisson + vertex colour transfer + optional photo_vertex_bake from originals.

capture_protocol.subject: Single rigid object on a table works best. Remove clutter; use a matte turntable or keep the camera moving and the object fixed.
capture_protocol.distance: Fill most of the frame with the object (PolyCam-style object mode). Too wide = weak texture on the object; too tight = no context for alignment.
capture_protocol.overlap: ~70–90% overlap between neighbouring views along the orbit. More views help more than higher resolution, up to server max_images.
capture_protocol.motion: Smooth arc around the object: low hemisphere (tabletop) plus a second higher ring for the top. Avoid single-axis spin only if the object is tall.
capture_protocol.exposure: Lock exposure/focus/WB across the burst (manual or AE-L). Harsh HDR or auto swings hurt multi-view consistency.
capture_protocol.motion_blur: Use short shutter / bright light; blur is lethal for neural SfM / GS.
capture_protocol.background: Prefer non-black, mildly textured backdrop for SIFT; SAM still isolates foreground. Plain white/black walls are harder—add paper clutter if needed.
capture_protocol.resolution: 4K uploads are OK; API downscales by max_input_image_side. Prefer stable 1080p–2K bursts with good exposure over noisy 8K.
capture_protocol.ordering: Time-ordered uploads match orbit order and often help matching stability.

web_ui_checklist.rule: Minimum 2 uploads (API). Block or warn heavily below 24 images for handheld object scans; 40+ is strongly recommended.
SAM default is center_point — show “keep object centered in frame” during capture/onboarding.
Warn if EXIF shutter is slow (>1/60 s) when available.
Upload images in capture order when possible.
After job starts, optionally link GET /jobs/{job_id}/... if you expose uploads; or tell users masks live under uploads/ with save_raw_masks (debug bad geometry).
Poll GET /jobs/{job_id}; label stages via GET /job-stages.
.ply: use a Gaussian Splatting viewer. .glb mesh: force vertex-colour/material mode (neutral grey ≠ missing colours if normals-only shader).

items: Show short copy from capture_protocol.overlap / motion / exposure (fetch GET /capture-guide).
Recommend two rings of photos (table height + slight elevation) around a fixed object.
Ask user to enable AE-lock / consistent exposure if the platform allows.
Display estimated image count; soft warning below 24, stronger below 18.
Optional: thumbnails in capture order with drag reorder.
Show max_images from GET /settings if over limit.
GET /job-stages once at app load; map job.stage base id to labels and progress bands.
When model_format is glb, hint: “If model looks grey, enable vertex colours in your viewer.”
When ply, link or embed a splat viewer (three.js splat, anti-aliased GS renderer, etc.).
GET /settings for admin; advanced users can merge recommended_settings_overlays from GET /capture-guide then PUT /settings.
After server upgrade, admins may DELETE or merge server config/runtime_settings.json to pick new server defaults—or PUT explicit fields.

recommended_settings_overlays._comment: Merge into your current settings: GET /settings, shallow-merge listed keys (replace only these), PUT /settings with the full validated body. Paths (sam_checkpoint_path, gs_repo_path) stay host-specific; install MapAnything pip package on workers.

gaussian_splatting_consumer_8gb.rationale: Lower VRAM during MapAnything scene seed on 8 GB.
Supervise GS with real colours—not SAM black padding.
Fast, predictable foreground when the object is centred (like guided capture).
Balance detail vs SAM/MapAnything/GS VRAM on 8 GB.
Softer than 3 for VRAM; raise to 3 for final renders if stable.
Better colour/geometry than 7k; increase to 20000–30000 for finals if heat/VRAM allow.
Allow more growth than 5k on warm GPUs; lower if OOM during densify.
When using .glb mesh path, photo-true vertex colours.

mesh_glb_friendly.rationale: Feed-forward metric mesh from masked views (Meta MapAnything).
Bake vertex RGB from originals when cameras succeed.
Matches default server cap; raise to 1920 for sharper bake if VRAM allows.
